sites.name: Charlotte Square
sites.tagline: Live above it all. Steps from everything.
sites.description: Leasing site for a LEED Gold building at 50 Charlotte Street in Rochester's East End. Residences and floor plans, amenities, neighborhood, tour scheduling and resident login, with the structured data, canonicals and technical SEO that make a property site rank. Tour requests route through a custom form into the company Google Workspace inbox and land in a live lead sheet, so leasing sees every enquiry with status, owner and follow-up in one place.

sites.name: Evolution24 Properties
sites.description: Corporate site for a family-owned property company: eleven buildings across Rochester, Syracuse, Manlius and Geneva, with live availability and rents from the same source the leasing team uses. Property pages for every building, an availability view, resident portal hand-off, FAQs and contact. Part of the same ecosystem as Charlotte Square and the company Google Workspace, so enquiries from any property route to the right inbox and the same lead sheet. Live at evolution24.net, replacing the company’s old WordPress site.

sites.name: IRL
sites.description: The no-algorithm social network: videos up to 11.11 seconds, photos, words, voice posts and notes from friends and family, newest first, in feeds that end with “You’re caught up.” No ads, no tracking, no human data sold, no follower counts for people, and seven feelings instead of likes. The Circle is your friends; the Square is everyone’s latest public post from the last 48 hours. Around them: IRL Radio, a people-powered station where a person listens to every track first, an Arcade of small games, Notes, groups, verified pages for local businesses and ten languages. Underneath is heavy cryptography: TLS 1.3 with the post-quantum X25519MLKEM768 key exchange over HTTP/3, passkeys instead of passwords, an Ed25519 Real Seal on every loop, and messages sealed with formally verified ChaCha20-Poly1305 from HACL*. The rules that keep bots out are model-checked in TLA+ across hundreds of thousands of states, and the algebra behind its one-time MAC is proven in Lean. Every post is checked before anyone sees it, people decide the hard cases, and a Sentinel programme traps and studies bots. Adults only, in the browser on any phone or computer.

sites.name: Round24
sites.description: The maintenance platform that measures the labor. Every hour, receipt and door reconciled automatically: Round24 turns the pay logs, rent rolls and P&L sheets a crew and office keep by hand into one connected, encrypted ledger, and gives residents a way in, so the whole building runs on one system. Built out of my own time in the field, with offline photo and receipt capture for techs with no signal in a basement. Live in beta.

sites.name: Bastion
sites.description: An open-source security sensor for Windows that runs alongside Microsoft Defender instead of replacing it. Bastion watches the surfaces Defender leaves alone: camera and mic access, USB drift, kernel-driver provenance, persistence changes and Defender's own tamper state. Every event is written to a tamper-evident merkle chain with a plain-language receipt, and a local console on 127.0.0.1 lets you kill, quarantine or trust a process from one screen, with a calm everyday view and a terminal-style operator view for triage. Nothing is sent off the machine. Access is donation-based, starting at free.

sites.name: cbuy
sites.tagline: Sell anything. Get paid in crypto.
sites.description: Peer-to-peer marketplace for physical goods, settled in stablecoins. Escrow releases on carrier delivery confirmation. Encrypted messaging, image verification, an AI price checker, barter, and a crypto sticker marketplace with an AI sticker maker. One flat fee, promised never to rise.

sites.name: Dot Trading Post
sites.tagline: Trade anything for anything. No money.
sites.description: A barter board for trading cards, video games, retro consoles, collectibles and NFTs, where nothing is bought or sold. Post what you have and what you'd take, and Dot looks for the person holding the other half, matching both ways and knowing PS5 and PlayStation 5 are the same thing. Swaps run physical for physical, NFT for NFT across chains, or physical for NFT. Same-chain NFT swaps settle in one transaction so nobody sends first, and agreed trades get four days to ship, tracking and a public no-show record. Reputation is counted in dots, worked out from the trade record itself, so they can't be bought or self-awarded. Private trade threads, location rounded to about a kilometre, and four languages. From the makers of cbuy.

sites.name: Faraday
sites.description: Anonymous encrypted video calling. A WebGL2 shader destroys your face and on-device DSP your voice before a byte leaves the browser. No accounts, no logs, no trackers. Relay-only TURN with ephemeral credentials, so your IP never reaches the peer. One-time fee, same code on every device.

sites.name: Glitch Pixel Studio
sites.tagline: Real-time WebGL glitch + AI camera FX.
sites.description: A real-time WebGL glitch and AI camera FX studio for Android. True CPU Asendorf pixel sort, GPU datamosh, kaleido and radial UV warps, 40+ generators, on-device MediaPipe face FX, MIDI and audio-reactive control, projector mode for VJ sets. The site itself runs a live shader kit you can play with.

sites.name: Scrawl
sites.description: A gallery for collectible fonts. Each minted release ties a 1/1 or fixed-edition collectible on Ethereum to working TTF, OTF and variable font files with a transferable licence, sold by zero-reserve ETH auction or buy-now. Artists get a public page and a studio: draw H, O and n with pixel, round, marker or texture brushes and Claude drafts the rest of the alphabet in that hand, or draw every glyph in the full editor. A reactive type lab animates variable fonts on width, slant and a custom Scrawl Pulse axis, and a foundry bot proposes three new alphabets every day for review. The founding gallery opened with 69 original designs.

sites.name: This Is An Art Gallery
sites.tagline: Anyone can hang work. Nobody signs it.
sites.description: An open, anonymous art gallery and minting platform on Base, curated in seasons by rotating directors. No artist names, no collector names: remove the name and the work has to stand on its own. Single 1/1 works with reserve auctions, a commissions program, a zine printed each season, and an open application flow.

sites.name: b0b.dev
sites.description: Independent OSINT research: sourced reporting on surveillance infrastructure and control networks, an interactive map, and open audio tools, all behind a video gate. Served with a strict content security policy and a crawler allowlist.
